plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud

Cost- and latency-reduction hybrid: keep the strongest model only for final user-facing answer generation, while moving routing, initial tool-control, and question rewriting to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, which supports both tool calling and structured output where required.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible because it lacks structured_output support. Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud instead of gpt-5.5-cloud to test a much lower-cost/lower-latency router while preserving required structured-output capability.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud on the final answer node to preserve answer quality on the user-facing synthesis step, which is directly reflected in exact match and token F1 metrics.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and controls the initial retrieval branch. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud satisfies tool-calling support and should substantially reduce cloud cost versus the baseline, while being stronger and safer than the local 2B model for branch decisions and possible direct responses.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rewrite is non-user-facing and does not require structured output or tools, but retrieval recovery quality can affect downstream answerability. Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud as a cheaper alternative to gpt-5.5-cloud without risking local-model degradation on query reformulation.

plan.description: Low-cost all-mini cloud placement: move final answer generation from gpt-5.5-cloud to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud while keeping all routing/control/rewrite units on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud. This is previously unevaluated and preserves required tool-calling and structured-output capabilities.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, making qwen-local ineligible because it lacks structured_output support. Candidate-1 showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud handled this router with much lower latency and cost than the all-gpt-5.5 baseline, so keep mini here.
rationale.generate_answer: Test the main remaining cost lever by replacing gpt-5.5-cloud with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud on final answer synthesis. In candidate-1, generate_answer accounted for about 85% of cloud cost despite only 50 invocations; all-mini should sharply reduce cost and likely latency, at the risk of measuring any quality drop on exact match/F1.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This unit requires tool calling and controls the initial retrieval branch. qwen-local supports tool calling, but it is user-facing and branch-critical; candidate-1 indicated gpt-4.1-mini-cloud produced strong overall quality with much lower latency/cost than gpt-5.5, so retain mini rather than introduce local risk yet.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing and no special endpoint capability requirements, but rewrite quality can affect recovery retrieval. Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud as in candidate-1 to maintain a consistent, cheap cloud controller/rewrite stack while isolating the experiment to final-answer model downgrade.

plan.description: Quality-recovery hybrid: keep the low-cost structured router and rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, restore gpt-5.5-cloud for the user-facing final answer and initial retrieval controller to test whether stronger first-pass tool/branch control recovers supporting evidence and answer quality while remaining cheaper/faster than the all-gpt-5.5 baseline.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This router requires structured output, so qwen-local is ineligible. Candidate-1 showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud can replace gpt-5.5-cloud here with large cost/latency savings and no obvious aggregate quality collapse; keep mini for this high-invocation non-user-facing branch decision.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-2 demonstrated a substantial quality drop when final synthesis was moved to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud (exact match 0.50 vs 0.68 in candidate-1 and 0.66 baseline; F1 0.647 vs 0.807/0.782). Restoring gpt-5.5-cloud isolates strong answer generation as the main quality-preserving lever.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This node is user-facing, tool-calling, and branch-critical. Candidate-1's all-mini control stack reduced cost/latency but had lower supporting-title metrics than the all-gpt-5.5 baseline, and candidate-2 further showed retrieval/support degradation. Use gpt-5.5-cloud here to test whether stronger initial retrieval decisions improve evidence selection and difficult-case quality, while still saving cost on the post-retrieval router and rewrite.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rewrite is non-user-facing and has no tool/structured requirement. Candidate-2 invoked it rarely and candidate-1 did not invoke it, so keeping gpt-4.1-mini-cloud here should minimize cost with limited expected impact; qwen-local is avoided for now to prevent introducing a new local-quality variable in the recovery experiment.

plan.description: Local-first controller experiment: keep the proven high-quality gpt-5.5-cloud final answer generator and the required structured post-retrieval router on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, while moving the initial tool-calling retrieval controller to qwen-local to test cloud-cost reduction on the most-invoked entry node. Keep rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud to avoid adding local rewrite-quality risk.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output for branch control. qwen-local is ineligible because it lacks structured_output support, while gpt-4.1-mini-cloud satisfied this requirement in candidates 1-3 at very low cost and latency relative to gpt-5.5-cloud. Retain mini here rather than reverting to the expensive baseline router.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-2 showed a large quality drop when final answer synthesis used gpt-4.1-mini-cloud (exact_match 0.50, F1 0.647) versus candidate-1 with gpt-5.5-cloud answers (exact_match 0.68, F1 0.807). Keep gpt-5.5-cloud on the user-facing synthesis node as the main quality-preserving component.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This node requires tool calling, which qwen-local supports, and it was the largest invocation-count node in every run. Candidate-1 demonstrated that gpt-4.1-mini-cloud control with gpt-5.5-cloud answers achieved the best observed aggregate quality/cost balance, while candidate-3 showed moving this node back to gpt-5.5-cloud worsened quality and increased cost. Testing qwen-local here explores an additional cloud-cost reduction lever while preserving tool capability and keeping downstream answer generation strong.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rewrite has no structured-output or tool-calling requirement, but query reformulation quality can influence retrieval recovery. Candidate-1 achieved strong quality with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud here and candidates showed rewrite is low-frequency; keep mini to isolate the experiment to the initial controller rather than confounding it with local rewrite behavior.

plan.description: Router-quality recovery probe: retain the strongest final answer generator and the low-cost/low-latency gpt-4.1-mini initial controller/rewrite stack from the best observed hybrid, but upgrade only the structured post-retrieval sufficiency router to gpt-5.5-cloud to test whether stronger relevance/completeness branch decisions recover supporting-title metrics or difficult-case answer quality without reverting to the high-cost all-gpt-5.5 baseline.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is not eligible. Candidate-1 used gpt-4.1-mini here and achieved the best observed exact_match/F1 balance, but supporting_title_hit/recall remained below the all-gpt-5.5 baseline. Upgrading only this router to gpt-5.5-cloud isolates whether stronger post-retrieval sufficiency decisions improve evidence routing and answerability, at lower incremental cost than also upgrading the initial controller.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud because candidate-2 showed a large quality drop when answer generation moved to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud (exact_match 0.50 and F1 0.647 versus candidate-1 exact_match 0.68 and F1 0.807). Final synthesis is user-facing and quality-critical.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because it supports tool calling and candidate-1 substantially reduced latency/cost while preserving the strongest aggregate quality observed. Candidate-3 showed that moving this initial controller to gpt-5.5-cloud increased cost and latency and degraded aggregate quality, while candidate-4 showed qwen-local increased latency and slightly reduced quality, so mini remains the clean control choice.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the non-user-facing rewrite. It is cheap, supports the needed context size, and avoids introducing local rewrite quality/latency variability while testing the single effect of a stronger post-retrieval router. This also preserves the candidate-1 rewrite setting for comparison.

plan.description: Isolated local-rewrite probe: preserve the strongest observed hybrid pattern for the structured router, final answer generation, and initial tool-calling controller, but move only the non-user-facing question rewrite unit to qwen-local. This tests whether the remaining rewrite step can be made zero-cloud-cost without materially affecting quality, while avoiding repeats of all evaluated assignment maps.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible because it lacks structured_output support. Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, which satisfied the structured-output requirement and delivered much lower cost/latency than gpt-5.5-cloud in prior hybrids; upgrading this router to gpt-5.5-cloud in candidate-5 increased cost and latency without improving exact match beyond candidate-1.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud on the user-facing final synthesis node. Candidate-2 showed a large quality regression when this unit moved to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, while candidates retaining gpt-5.5-cloud for final answers achieved the best exact_match and token-F1 results.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the initial tool-calling retrieval controller. It supports tool calling and candidate-1 achieved the best observed aggregate quality/cost/latency balance with this setting; moving this unit to gpt-5.5-cloud in candidate-3 worsened quality and increased cost, while moving it to qwen-local in candidate-4 increased latency and slightly reduced quality.
rationale.rewrite_question: Move only this non-user-facing, no-tool, no-structured-output unit to qwen-local. Prior runs show rewrite is low-frequency, so this is a low-risk way to test whether local rewrite can eliminate the remaining small rewrite cloud cost while preserving the candidate-1 control/answer stack. qwen-local has sufficient context window and no incompatible capability requirement for this unit.

plan.description: Question-rewrite quality probe: preserve the strongest observed control/answer pattern from the best hybrid runs—gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the structured post-retrieval router and initial tool-calling controller, plus gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer synthesis—but upgrade only the non-user-facing rewrite step to gpt-5.5-cloud. This previously unevaluated placement tests whether stronger rewrite quality helps recovery cases without changing the high-impact routing/controller/answer assignments.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This post-retrieval router requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Prior runs indicate gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is the best cost/latency choice here: candidate-1 achieved the strongest aggregate exact_match/F1 balance with mini on this unit, while candidate-5's upgrade of this router to gpt-5.5-cloud increased cost and latency without improving exact match beyond candidate-1.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud on final answer generation because it is user-facing and quality-critical. Candidate-2 showed that moving answer synthesis to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud sharply reduced quality (exact_match 0.50 and F1 about 0.647 versus candidate-1 exact_match 0.68 and F1 about 0.807), while hybrids with gpt-5.5-cloud answers were the strongest observed quality configurations.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the initial retrieval controller because it supports tool calling and delivered the best observed quality/cost/latency balance in candidate-1. Moving this unit to gpt-5.5-cloud in candidate-3 increased cost and degraded quality, while moving it to qwen-local in candidate-4 produced slower latency and slightly lower quality than candidate-1.
rationale.rewrite_question: Upgrade only the rewrite unit to gpt-5.5-cloud. Rewriting is non-user-facing and does not require tool calling or structured output, so all endpoints are capability-compatible; however candidate-6's local rewrite probe underperformed candidate-1, and prior runs show rewrite can affect recovery behavior despite low invocation counts. This isolates whether the strongest model improves reformulation on hard retrieval cases while adding limited expected cost because rewrite is usually invoked infrequently.

plan.description: Local final-answer cost probe: keep the strongest observed low-cost cloud control stack from candidate-1/candidate-2 for structured routing, initial tool-calling retrieval control, and rewrite, but move only user-facing final answer generation to qwen-local. This previously unevaluated placement tests the extreme cloud-cost reduction lever after candidate-2 showed that downgrading final answers to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud greatly reduced cost/latency but hurt quality.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Prior runs consistently showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is the most attractive structured router: candidate-1 achieved the best observed exact_match/F1 balance with mini here, while candidate-5's gpt-5.5-cloud router increased cost and latency without improving exact match over candidate-1.
rationale.generate_answer: Move final answer generation to qwen-local as a previously unevaluated cost/latency-quality stress test. Candidate-1 and related hybrids indicate gpt-5.5-cloud is quality-preserving but dominates cloud cost, while candidate-2 showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud final answers cut cost sharply but reduced exact_match from 0.68 to 0.50. qwen-local is capability-compatible for this no-tool, unstructured generation unit and tests whether any acceptable answer quality can be retained with zero cloud cost on the synthesis step.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the initial retrieval controller because it supports tool calling and produced the best observed quality/cost/latency balance in candidate-1. Moving this unit to gpt-5.5-cloud in candidate-3 degraded aggregate quality and increased cost, while moving it to qwen-local in candidate-4 increased latency and slightly reduced quality, so mini is the stable control choice while isolating the final-answer experiment.
rationale.rewrite_question: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for rewrite to avoid confounding the local final-answer test with rewrite changes. Candidate-6's qwen-local rewrite assignment underperformed candidate-1, and candidate-7's gpt-5.5-cloud rewrite did not materially beat candidate-1 while costing more; mini remains the measured low-risk rewrite setting.

plan.description: Mini final-answer with upgraded post-retrieval router probe: keep the low-cost gpt-4.1-mini-cloud stack for initial tool-calling retrieval control and rewrite, use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for final answer generation to preserve the low-cost/low-latency profile seen in all-mini, but upgrade only the structured retrieval-sufficiency router to gpt-5.5-cloud. This previously unevaluated placement isolates whether stronger post-retrieval branch decisions can improve the evidence quality and downstream answerability of the low-cost final-answer setting.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Candidate-2 showed the all-mini stack was very cheap and fast but had reduced answer quality and supporting-title metrics; candidate-5 showed gpt-5.5-cloud can serve this structured router, though at higher cost. Upgrading only this router while keeping mini final answers tests whether stronger sufficiency decisions recover retrieval/evidence quality in the low-cost answer regime.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud to explore a lower-cost, lower-latency alternative to gpt-5.5-cloud on the user-facing answer step. Candidate-2 showed quality dropped versus gpt-5.5 answer generation, but it also delivered the lowest all-cloud cost and latency; pairing mini answers with a stronger router is a new trade-off point not yet measured.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because it supports tool calling and has been the most reliable low-cost initial controller in prior runs. Candidate-3's gpt-5.5-cloud controller increased cost/latency and degraded aggregate quality, while candidate-4's qwen-local controller increased latency and slightly reduced quality relative to the mini-controller hybrid, so mini remains the best control choice for this experiment.
rationale.rewrite_question: Keep rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud to avoid confounding this test with local or gpt-5.5 rewrite changes. Candidate-6's local rewrite underperformed and candidate-7's gpt-5.5 rewrite did not materially improve over the mini rewrite setting; mini is capability-compatible, inexpensive, and the stable baseline for rewrite.

plan.description: Local initial-controller with upgraded structured sufficiency router: keep qwen-local on the high-invocation tool-calling entry node to retain the cloud-cost reduction explored in candidate-4, keep gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer quality, and upgrade only the post-retrieval structured router to gpt-5.5-cloud to test whether stronger sufficiency decisions recover quality/supporting-evidence metrics lost by the local controller. Rewrite remains on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud as a low-cost, stable setting.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Candidate-4 showed that using qwen-local for the initial controller with a mini router preserved reasonable quality at moderate cloud cost, while candidate-5 showed a gpt-5.5-cloud router is expensive but can support strong answer-quality settings. Upgrading the router here isolates whether stronger relevance/completeness decisions can compensate for local initial retrieval control.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-5.5-cloud because final answer generation is user-facing and prior measurements show this is the main quality-preserving lever: candidate-2 and candidate-8 suffered large quality drops when final synthesis moved to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud or qwen-local, whereas gpt-5.5-cloud answer hybrids achieved the strongest exact-match/F1 results.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use qwen-local for this tool-calling entry node. It supports tools and candidate-4 demonstrated a meaningful cloud-call/cost reduction with only a modest quality decrease versus candidate-1, although with higher latency. Keeping qwen here tests whether the upgraded downstream router can improve candidate-4's quality while retaining zero cloud cost on the most-invoked controller.
rationale.rewrite_question: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for rewrite because it is capability-compatible, low-cost, and comparatively stable. Candidate-6's qwen-local rewrite underperformed and candidate-7's gpt-5.5-cloud rewrite did not materially improve over mini, so using mini avoids adding another variable while testing the router upgrade.

plan.description: Local controller plus local rewrite probe with strong answer synthesis: keep gpt-5.5-cloud for final user-facing answer quality and gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the required structured post-retrieval router, while moving both tool-capable initial retrieval control and non-structured rewrite to qwen-local to explore additional cloud-cost reduction versus candidate-4 without repeating any evaluated assignment map.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, making qwen-local ineligible because it lacks structured_output support. Prior runs show gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is the best low-cost structured router: candidate-1 achieved the strongest observed aggregate quality/cost balance with mini here, while upgrading this router to gpt-5.5-cloud in candidates 5, 9, and 10 greatly increased cost/latency without a clear quality win.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-5.5-cloud because final answer generation is user-facing and has been the main quality-preserving lever. Candidate-2's mini final answers and candidate-8's local final answers produced large quality drops, whereas hybrids retaining gpt-5.5-cloud for final synthesis generally delivered the best exact-match and token-F1 results.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use qwen-local for the initial retrieval controller to continue exploring cloud-cost reduction on the high-invocation, tool-calling entry node; qwen-local supports tool calling and has sufficient context. Candidate-4 showed local control with strong final answers remained reasonably competitive in quality, though slower, and this placement tests that setting combined with local rewrite rather than the previously evaluated mini rewrite.
rationale.rewrite_question: Move rewrite to qwen-local because this unit is non-user-facing and requires neither tools nor structured output, so qwen-local is capability-compatible. Although candidate-6's isolated local rewrite underperformed, rewrite invocation is typically low and this new pairing with a local initial controller tests whether eliminating rewrite cloud cost/latency from the candidate-4-style stack changes the trade-off without repeating an evaluated assignment.

plan.description: Low-cloud-cost local-entry / mini-answer probe: keep the required structured post-retrieval router and rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, move the high-invocation tool-calling entry controller to qwen-local, and use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for final answer generation. This previously unevaluated placement explores a more aggressive cost-reduction point than candidate-4/candidate-11 by also downgrading final synthesis from gpt-5.5-cloud, while avoiding the very poor local final-answer setting from candidate-8.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This retrieval sufficiency router requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Prior evaluations show gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is the lower-cost structured router: candidate-1 achieved the strongest observed quality/cost balance with mini here, while gpt-5.5-cloud router variants such as candidates 5, 9, and 10 increased cost/latency without a clear aggregate quality win.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud rather than gpt-5.5-cloud to test a cheaper final synthesis setting in combination with a local entry controller. Candidate-2 showed mini answers reduce quality versus gpt-5.5 answers but provide very low cost and latency, while candidate-8 showed local final answers are too damaging. Mini is therefore the more plausible low-cost answer endpoint for this trade-off probe.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use qwen-local on the high-invocation entry node because it supports tool calling and has sufficient context. Candidate-4 and candidate-11 showed local initial control can retain moderate quality while reducing cloud calls/cost versus mini-controller hybrids, although with latency risk. Pairing it with mini answer generation creates a new, more cost-focused placement not yet evaluated.
rationale.rewrite_question: Keep rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud as the stable low-cost rewrite setting. Candidate-6's isolated qwen-local rewrite and candidate-7's gpt-5.5 rewrite did not improve the measured trade-off over mini rewrite, so mini avoids adding another variable while testing the combined local-entry and mini-answer cost reduction.
